name: YouTube — Unofficial OTR Channels
operator: Google / Alphabet + Hundreds of Unaffiliated Uploaders

pricing.billingNote: Free tier injects jarring mid-roll video ads every 6–10 minutes unless paying $13.99/mo for YouTube Premium.
pricing.freeTierNote: Ad-supported streaming with mid-roll interruptions and locked screen playback restrictions on mobile.

formats: Opus / AAC inside MP4/WebM Video Container

provenance.primaryMasterSource: Re-encoded collector MP3s muxed with AI-generated static images and heavy loudness normalization
provenance.airdateMethodology: Rampant clickbait/AI-invented dates or stripped dates ('RARE Episode You Never Heard!')
provenance.castAttributionMethod: Rarely credited; often hallucinates famous actors in clickbait thumbnails
provenance.captionEngine: YouTube Auto-ASR (low accuracy on 1940s transatlantic dialects & vintage sponsor names)

specNotes.ad_free: Injects loud programmatic pre-roll and mid-roll video ads unless paying $13.99/mo ($167.88/yr) for YouTube Premium.

primary_source_verification.summary: Uploaders routinely strip real air dates and original episode titles in favor of clickbait titles to game recommendation algorithms.
primary_source_verification.evidenceQuote: "Channels frequently rename canonical broadcasts to 'Chilling 1940s Detective Mystery!' to prevent viewers from realizing they've already heard it."

cast_credit_accuracy.summary: Thumbnails frequently paste photos of Humphrey Bogart, Orson Welles, or Vincent Price onto episodes in which they never appeared.
cast_credit_accuracy.evidenceQuote: "AI-generated thumbnails and video titles routinely misattribute series stars for clickthrough rate."

vtt_transcripts.summary: YouTube auto-captions exist on most uploads, but lack punctuation, speaker separation, and proper-noun accuracy for 1930s–1950s radio.
vtt_transcripts.evidenceQuote: "Automated YouTube ASR captions are available via the CC button, though unedited and prone to period-name mistranscriptions."

master_provenance.summary: Audio is typically a 32–64k collector MP3 re-compressed through video editing software, brick-walled with heavy compression, and re-encoded by YouTube.
master_provenance.evidenceQuote: "Multiple lossy transcode generations (MP3 → AAC video render → YouTube Opus/AAC) plus aggressive dynamic range compression."

serial_continuity.summary: Algorithmic autoplay shuffles unrelated shows and breaks multi-part serial story arcs.
serial_continuity.evidenceQuote: "YouTube's recommendation sidebar and autoplay queue prioritize engagement metrics over chronological broadcast sequence."

open_api_export.summary: YouTube Data API v3 is strictly quota-capped, prohibits audio downloading in ToS, and offers no OTR relational schema.
open_api_export.evidenceQuote: "YouTube Terms of Service prohibit direct audio stream extraction or bulk archival mirroring."

ad_free_playback.summary: Monetized channels insert loud modern video ads every 6–10 minutes right in the middle of 1940s radio dramas unless paying $13.99/mo.
ad_free_playback.evidenceQuote: "Mid-roll ad breaks at +0 dBFS interrupt quiet vintage broadcasts unless the listener subscribes to YouTube Premium ($13.99/mo)."

dedup_integrity.summary: The same 500 popular episodes of *CBSRMT*, *Suspense*, and *Yours Truly Johnny Dollar* are re-uploaded hundreds of times under disguised titles.
dedup_integrity.evidenceQuote: "Massive duplication across '8-Hour Old Time Radio Sleep' compilation videos with zero canonical broadcast IDs."

gotchas.title: Loud Mid-Roll Ads Spliced Into Quiet 1940s Drama Scenes
gotchas.detail: Unless you pay $13.99/mo ($139.99/yr) for YouTube Premium, modern high-LUFS commercials blast at random intervals during suspenseful scenes.

gotchas.title: Deliberate Title & Air Date Obfuscation
gotchas.detail: Many monetized OTR channels intentionally delete the real broadcast date and episode title so listeners cannot tell it is a re-upload.

gotchas.title: Mobile Background Playback Paywalled
gotchas.detail: Turning off your phone screen to listen to a radio show stops playback on mobile unless paying for YouTube Premium.
